I love pinball games and have been playing them since my grade school days. To get a pinball video game right is a difficult task. You either lean too far into gimmicks that it doesn't feel like pinball or strip it down so much there's little left than launch and lose. This hits that perfect sweet spot. It takes full advantage of its special effects and practical pinball basics to make easily one of the best digital tables I've ever played.  I used to play a gameboy title called Revenge of the Gator. Simple but had the same table layout of a top, middle, and lower playfield with portals to special stages. Not since that game was in my hands in the 90s have I felt anything as fun or creative, then Demon's Tilt came on my radar.
It's a neoclassical game. Taking what was done in the past, repeating and adding onto it. If you like pinball and are looking for something new and exciting, this is it. 10/10

While not having the whole table visible at once and the camera movement is a jarring experience and makes multiball especially difficult, the table itself is quite an enjoyable and packed. The moving enemies and their projectile attacks interacting with the ball can really feel unfair on your first few plays, but once you understand that active nudging is intended as a way to interact with the enemies (the tilt sensor is very forgiving) and not just a way of tweaking shot angles and lane saves, it becomes a great added level of complexity to gameplay. If you find yourself with hundreds of hours of traditional virtual pinball under your belt and looking for something a bit different to shake things up, this satisfies that need without being a complete departure from the typical pinball play loop.

A unique experience in the digital pinball genre. Don't go into this one expecting a pinball sim. Demon's tilt is far from it - and that's part of the charm. 

Demon's tilt is like an arcadey pinball bullet hell. It can be a bit daunting, disorienting, and downright confusing on the first few balls. As you learn the board and the mechanics, it'll come together and is a ton of fun. Anyone can pick up Demon's tilt and have a good time, but it will take hours to master the mechanics of the table and using your tilt correctly. 

The game doesn't go on sale very often and I do feel it is a bit pricey for essentially one table (even if that one table is more like 3 small tables). So I am not sure I would recommend Demon's tilt to EVERYONE. However, if you are a pinball enthusiast or this game looks intriguing to you. Definitely give it a shot.
